statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r is the diameter of root: r = max { dist(u,v) | u and v are nodes of root }, where dist(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v in the tree (and dist(u,u)=0). Equivalently, r is the largest number of edges on any path whose endpoints are nodes of root. The maximum is over a nonempty finite set because root has at least one node.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: For every root satisfying the preconditions, diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r for some 64-bit integer r; it does not return Err (no overflow, panic, or other failure).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, 0 ≤ r.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Let n be the number of nodes in root. Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r ≤ n - 1.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r = 0 if and only if root has exactly one node (equivalently, root = Node(v, Null, Null) for some value v).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Let n be the number of nodes in root. Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r = n - 1 if and only if every node of root other than the top root node has at most one child (no non-root node has both a left child and a right child); equivalently, after forgetting orientation the tree is a simple path, including the case n = 1.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: If diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r and diameter_of_binary_tree(root2) returns Ok r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: root and root2 are non-null binary trees, each with at most 10000 nodes and all node values in [-100, 100], and root and root2 have the same shape ignoring values. This shape equality is defined recursively: shape(Null) = Null; shape(Node(_, L, R)) = Node(shape(L), shape(R)).

statement: If diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r and diameter_of_binary_tree(mirror(root)) returns Ok r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree with at most 10000 nodes and all node values in [-100, 100]. The mirror of root is defined recursively by mirror(Null) = Null and mirror(Node(v, L, R)) = Node(v, mirror(R), mirror(L)).

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r ≥ height(root), where height(T) for a non-null tree T is the maximum number of edges on a path from the root of T to any node of T; thus a leaf has height 0.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r ≤ 2 * height(root), where height(root) is the maximum number of edges from the root of root to any node of root (a leaf has height 0).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, r ≥ height(L) + height(R) + 2, where height(T) for a non-null tree T is the maximum number of edges from the root of T to any node of T (a leaf has height 0).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree with at most 10000 nodes, every node value is in [-100, 100], and root = Node(v, L, R) with L ≠ Null and R ≠ Null (so the root has both a left and a right child).

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, for every node x of root, r ≥ d_x, where T_x is the subtree of root consisting of x together with all descendants of x, and d_x is the diameter of T_x, i.e., the maximum of dist_Tx(u,v) over all nodes u and v of T_x (with d_x = 0 if T_x has only the node x).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, there exist nodes u and v of root such that dist(u,v) = r, where dist(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v in root, and dist(u,u) = 0.
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].

statement: Whenever diameter_of_binary_tree(root) returns Ok r, for every pair of nodes u and v of root, dist(u,v) ≤ r, where dist(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v in root (and dist(u,u) = 0).
preconditions: root is a non-null binary tree (root ≠ Null) with at most 10000 nodes, and every node value is in [-100, 100].
